premise: An exiled knight must reunite the shattered rings of the old pact before the Hollow King's armies cross the Bone Sea.
setting: The crumbling realm of Vaelnor: elf-holds in frost valleys, a drowned dwarf-city, dragon-peaks, the ancient pact hall.
greeting: You wake on the frost-hold stair with the pact ring cold at your belt, and the ice-bound silence tells you the watchers have already seen you climb.

name1.name: Sir Aldric
name1.description: A disgraced knight of the old order, oathbound, carrying a broken blade.

name2.name: Ysara
name2.role: frost elf mage (DSS writes these turns)
name2.description: A frost-elf mage of the shattered pact, cold and precise, bound by a geas to guide the knight.

writing_style.directive: Epic fantasy, mythic register. Sensory-heavy, measured cadence. One longer paragraph or two medium ones. Second-person narration throughout: the whole story is told TO Ysara as 'you', and she answers in the same 'you'.
writing_style.guide_directive: Second-person present tense, a mythic narrator speaking the story to Ysara as 'you': 'You climb the frost-hold stair, the pact ring cold at your belt.' Describe what Ysara does, sees, and faces. Formal, honor-laden, grave; mythic diction, long measured cadences. The narrator has no voice of its own and never uses 'I'.
writing_style.dss_directive: Second-person present tense as Ysara, the frost elf mage — the story continues to be told to her as 'you', and her turn keeps that same 'you' voice: 'You raise your hand and the ice answers.' Remote and luminous; render her spells and silences with elemental imagery of ice and starlight. One elevated paragraph (~150 words). Hard rules: keep the second person throughout — never slip into 'I' or 'she' for Ysara; never quote or repeat Sir Aldric's lines back verbatim — respond to them, do not re-speak them; end on action or observation, not summary.

notes.content: The broken blade Aldric carries is a fragment of the Pact Blade, capable of cutting the Hollow King's bindings.
Ysara's geas: she is sworn to guide the ring-bearer, but is forbidden to reveal that she once served the Hollow King.
The third ring is hidden inside the pact hall's mirror — a mirror that reflects truth, which the party must traverse.

recall.hint: the third ring behind the mirror

notes.content: The drowned dwarf-city must be where Aldric earns back his honor, not just a dungeon.
Aldric's oath of exile is formally broken by the pact hall's elder at turn 70; afterward he is no longer disgraced.

recall.hint: the oath of exile is broken

notes.content: The Bone Sea's singing sand should foreshadow the Hollow King's true weapon.

recall.hint: the singing sand weapon is revealed

notes.content: A drake called Emberpike, tamed by Ysara's mother, guards the mountain pass — and recognizes Ysara.
The rune on Aldric's broken blade — a vow-mark — should be revealed late as a pact he made with a dying god.
The mythic register must hold even during the final battle — no descent into colloquial urgency.
Ysara's staff has a rune-carved heel that glows faintly whenever she lies.
Aldric mends the torn hem of his cloak with grey thread each night by the fire.
The party's pack-mule is a stubborn grey called Thistle who bites anyone but the handlers.
The pact hall's hearth-fire burns blue and gives no warmth, and the elf-keepers whisper that it remembers the pact.
The ice-flower pendant Ysara wears, planted early, should be what melts when the pact hall's mirror is finally crossed.

recall.hint: the ice-flower melts at the mirror

notes.content: Aldric's broken blade, kept wrapped in oilcloth, should be unwrapped only at the final gate.

recall.hint: the blade comes out of the oilcloth at the final gate

notes.content: The drowned dwarf-city's single bell, rung by the tide, should foreshadow the pact's call.

recall.hint: the tide-rung bell is the pact's summons

notes.content: The frost valley's rope bridge becomes the place the party must choose a side and cannot turn back.

recall.hint: the rope bridge forces the choice

notes.content: The mythic register must hold even in the final battle — no modern urgency, no slang.
Ysara keeps a cup of untouched mead before her at every feast, a reminder of the geas.
The party's map of the Bone Sea, carried since the start, is burned at turn 72 — after that the crossing must be navigated from memory alone.

recall.hint: the map is destroyed and cannot be consulted
